Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 reads 'exequatur' where the 1962 reads 'exsequatur' (the 1604 also reads 'exequatur'); conclusion is the same short cue 'Per Dominum.' in both; pointing otherwise identical, semicolon after 'tuae' included. Per Dominum.' Degraded-latin witness, corroboration only.. Recorded limitation: The 1862 layer damages two words: it reads 'tuani' for 'tuam' (minim confusion) at line 20201 and 'prasta' for 'praesta' at 20203, and the ornamental D is mangled as 'TYEus' / 'JL/'. I inferred those letterforms rather than read them; both are printed unambiguously at the same place in the 1604 at 16277-16281. All 1862 readings here rest on the tracked whole-book text layer alone; no page image of the 1862 is available to this lane and none was read. The 1862's 'Aliae Orationes, ut in Feria iv. Cinerum' pointer at 20209-20210 is that book's own pre-1955 matter and was not taken.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Sacrificium quadragesimalis initii solemniter immolamus, te, Domine,
deprecantes: ut, cum epularum restrictione carnalium, a noxiis quoque
voluptatibus temperemus. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
